title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's letter to John Coates, dated 6.1.1966 (possibly a slip for 1967), commenting on his talk on the standard conjectures. Notation: X is smooth projective of dimension n, Y a smooth hyperplane section, L_X the Lefschetz operator, Λ_X its (conjecturally algebraic) inverse. From the proof, C_χ(X) is the Lefschetz-type condition: the inverse of L^{n-i}: H^i → H^{2n-i} is algebraic. This is what the Bombay paper later calls B(X). D_χ means homological = numerical equivalence.

The Proposition (previous page) says C_χ(X) is equivalent to (b): (i) every algebraic endomorphism of H^i(X) has a characteristic polynomial with rational coefficients, and (ii) for each i<n there is some algebraic isomorphism u: H^{2n-i} → H^i.

End of proof. Let v = L^{n-i} and w = uv, an algebraic automorphism of H^i. By Cayley–Hamilton, w^{-1} is a polynomial in w with coefficients ±σ_k(w)/σ_b(w), which are rational. So w^{-1} is algebraic, and hence so is v^{-1} = w^{-1}u. Consequently C_χ does not depend on the polarization.

NB. In characteristic 0, hypothesis (i) is automatic: correspondences act on rational Betti cohomology. So C(X) is equivalent to the mere existence of algebraic isomorphisms H^{2n-i} → H^i. He hopes the same holds in arbitrary characteristic.

Corollary. If X and X' satisfy C_χ and u: H^i(X) → H^{i+2p}(X') is an algebraic isomorphism, then u^{-1} is algebraic. Proof: Poincaré duality composed with the algebraic Lefschetz isomorphism (and its algebraic inverse) identifies each space with its dual algebraically in both directions. So the transpose of u gives an algebraic u': H^{i+2p}(X') → H^i(X). Then w = u'u is an algebraic automorphism, w^{-1} is algebraic by Cayley–Hamilton, and u^{-1} = w^{-1}u'. Consequence for i even: if u(x) is algebraic then x is algebraic.

Sketched extension to monomorphisms. One needs an algebraic left inverse. This exists for the restriction φ*: H^{n-1}(X) → H^{n-1}(Y), namely Λ_X φ_*, since φ_*φ* = L_X. In general it seems to need the Hodge index relation. The yoga is that C(X) + I(X×X) imply that the algebra of correspondence classes is semisimple, which yields algebraic one-sided inverses; ultimately, motives form a semisimple category. He proposes an extra paragraph in the notes for this and for deducing Weil from C and A.
errors: 'Of course C_χ(X) implies a)' requires D_χ(X). Lefschetz-type B(X) is not known to imply D(X) in general (known: D(X×X) ⇒ B(X), and B + Hodge index ⇒ D). So either C_χ in the talk included D, or this step is a gap. It does not affect the substantive direction b) ⇒ C_χ.

The preliminary condition (i) of b) is in fact implied by C_χ itself without D. Lefschetz implies the Künneth components are algebraic, so tr(w^k|H^i) is an intersection number, hence rational, and Newton's identities give rational σ_k. So b) follows from C_χ directly.

In the Corollary, applying the Cayley–Hamilton argument to w requires rationality of the characteristic polynomial. This is supplied by C_χ(X) through the Künneth argument just described, but it is left implicit.
Minor: the NB calls char 0 simplification 'C(X)' while elsewhere writing C_χ(X); notation is slightly inconsistent.

ideas.what: Lefschetz standard conjecture is independent of polarization and equivalent to the existence of any algebraic isomorphism H^{2n-i} → H^i (given rational characteristic polynomials), via Cayley–Hamilton

ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) mentions polarization independence; detailed proofs in Kleiman 1968/1994

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether, in positive characteristic, B(X) is equivalent to the bare existence of algebraic isomorphisms H^{2n-i} → H^i without the rationality hypothesis. Via the trace argument this follows from the Künneth conjecture. Hence it holds for X over a finite field by Katz–Messing (1974), but it remains open over general fields of characteristic p.
missed.quote: Maybe with some extra care this can be proved too in arbitrary characteristics.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Small, known-to-experts remark. It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Cayley–Hamilton arguments around the Lefschetz standard conjecture. They appear (in substance) in Kleiman's expositions and André's book. The letter is a nice source showing Grothendieck's own early formulations, including the semisimplicity yoga, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
